outcome: Prevalence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
Maternal outcomes (e.g., cesarean section, instrumental deliveries)
Fetal outcomes (e.g., preterm birth, low birth weight, Apgar scores, stillbirth)
cohort: 615 women who attended delivery at Yekatit-12 Teaching Hospital from July 1, 2017, to January 1, 2018
finding: The prevalence of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy was high (25.4%) and was associated with adverse maternal and fetal outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and stillbirth.
mod_finding: Mothers with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were more likely to require interventions to terminate the pregnancy, either by cesarean section (42.3%) or instrumental deliveries (3.7%).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was reported as an outcome, but specific weight categories were not mentioned.
